Course Organization
This section is completed by the Author
1
Terminal Objective: Apply Codex to plan and execute a codebase refactoring operation using reviewable passes
1a. Construct a refactoring prompt that instructs Codex to map noisy modules, identify dead code, and propose one cleanup theme at a time before editing
1b. Apply the ExecPlan pattern to maintain a running log of intended changes, behavior contracts, and validation checks across a multi-session refactor
1c. Evaluate a Codex-generated refactoring diff to confirm that public behavior is preserved and that architecture migrations are separated into discrete tasks
1d. Explain when to use Plan mode before committing Codex to implementation
Terminal Objective: Demonstrate how to orchestrate a legacy-to-modern stack migration with Codex using incremental checkpoints.
2a. Direct Codex to inventory a legacy system's routing, data models, auth, build tooling, tests, and external contracts before proposing a migration plan
2b. Evaluate a Codex-generated migration plan for compatibility layers, explicit behavioral exceptions, and rollback visibility
2c. Apply validation checks (lint, type-check, focused tests) after each migration milestone rather than batching cleanup
2d. Use the ASP.NET Core skill or equivalent framework skill to apply platform-specific migration guidance
Module 1 – Refactoring and migrating codebases with Codex
Clip 1: Plan reviewable refactors with Codex (3 minutes)
•  Use Plan mode when discovery and architectural understanding should happen before implementation
•  Map the review flow from codebase evidence to bounded cleanup theme, implementation, validation, and diff review
•  Keep behavior preservation and architecture migrations as separate review decisions
•  Learning Objectives: TO1, EO1d
Clip 2: Demo: Map noisy TypeScript modules with Codex before editing (6 minutes)
•  Open the TypeScript service in Codex and ask it to map modules, dependencies, public behavior, and dead-code candidates
•  Constrain Codex to propose one cleanup theme before editing any files
•  Inspect repository evidence and reject unrelated architectural changes before implementation
•  Confirm Plan mode produces a bounded, reviewable first pass
•  Learning Objectives: TO1, EO1a, EO1d
Clip 3: Demo: Execute a Codex refactor with ExecPlan checkpoints (6 minutes)
•  Create an ExecPlan that records intended changes, behavior contracts, validation checks, and progress across the refactor
•  Let Codex implement one bounded cleanup pass and run Vitest plus TypeScript validation
•  Inspect the generated diff and confirm public behavior is preserved
•  Remove the architecture migration Codex bundled into the cleanup diff and log it as a separate ExecPlan task
•  Learning Objectives: TO1, EO1b, EO1c
Clip 4: Plan a legacy Express migration with Codex checkpoints (3 minutes)
•  Shift from the refactoring project to the legacy CommonJS JavaScript Express 4 service and define ESM TypeScript on Express 5 as the target
•  Separate inventory, CommonJS-to-ESM compatibility planning, validation, and rollback into explicit checkpoints before implementation
•  Treat behavioral exceptions and the CommonJS-to-ESM compatibility layer as deliberate migration decisions
•  Learning Objectives: TO2
Clip 5: Demo: Inventory a legacy Express 4 service with Codex (6 minutes)
•  Direct Codex to inventory the legacy CommonJS JavaScript Express 4 service across Express routes, data models, auth, build tooling, tests, and external contracts
•  Review the generated migration plan for the CommonJS-to-ESM compatibility layer, explicit behavioral exceptions, and rollback visibility
•  Split the ESM TypeScript Express 5 migration into incremental milestones that can be validated independently
•  Reject the milestone that batches route migration with dependency upgrades and have Codex split it into two checkpoints
•  Learning Objectives: TO2, EO2a, EO2b
Clip 6: Demo: Migrate one Express route to TypeScript with framework guidance (6 minutes)
•  Apply an equivalent Node.js and TypeScript framework skill to migrate one Express route slice from JavaScript to TypeScript
•  Run ESLint, TypeScript type-checking, build validation, and focused Vitest tests immediately after the route migration
•  Inspect the diff and verify the CommonJS-to-ESM compatibility contract before accepting the route change
•  Record the checkpoint so the Express 5 migration can continue or roll back from a known state
•  Learning Objectives: TO2, EO2c, EO2d
30 Mins
2
Terminal Objective: Apply Codex automations to run recurring bug triage across multiple data sources at team scale.
3a. Configure a bug triage automation using the Sentry, Slack, Linear, and GitHub plugins to sweep a defined time window
3b. Evaluate a Codex-generated triage report for correct P0–P3 prioritization, deduplicated bug entries, and evidence-backed recommendations
3c. Convert a tested manual triage sweep into a scheduled automation using the same thread context
3d. Apply a routing workflow to draft Slack updates, Linear issues, or GitHub comments after triage approval
Terminal Objective:  Demonstrate how to debug and trace Codex automations
4a. Use the Codex review pane to inspect uncommitted diffs from an automation run, including per-hunk staging and revert controls
Module 2 – Automating and debugging Codex workflows at team scale
Clip 1: Design reviewable Codex automations at team scale (3 minutes)
•  Map the triage architecture from Sentry and GitHub evidence through correlation, P0–P3 prioritization, review, approval, and routed drafts to Slack and Linear
•  Keep source evidence attached to each P0–P3 recommendation so team decisions remain reviewable
•  Separate approved downstream actions from the triage decision itself
•  Learning Objectives: TO3
Clip 2: Demo: Run a manual Codex triage sweep across Sentry and GitHub (6 minutes)
•  Configure Sentry and GitHub evidence sources, connect Slack and Linear routing destinations, and define the triage time window
•  Run the sweep manually so the same thread context captures source evidence before scheduling
•  Inspect the report for P0–P3 priority, deduplicated bugs, and evidence-backed recommendations
•  Correct weak prioritization or duplicate entries before automation is promoted
•  Learning Objectives: TO3, EO3a, EO3b
Clip 3: Demo: Schedule Codex triage and route work to Slack and Linear (6 minutes)
•  Convert the tested manual sweep into a scheduled Codex automation using the same thread context
•  Run the scheduled workflow and compare its report with the validated manual pattern
•  Approve selected findings before drafting Slack updates or Linear issues
•  Verify Slack and Linear drafts preserve the evidence and priority from the triage decision
•  Learning Objectives: TO3, EO3c, EO3d
Clip 4: Debug Codex automations through review evidence (3 minutes)
•  Use automation inputs, generated changes, validation results, and review state as the debugging evidence chain
•  Distinguish a bad source assumption from a bad generated change before deciding what to rerun
•  Use per-hunk review to keep valid changes while rejecting unsafe or unrelated edits
•  Learning Objectives: TO4, EO4a
Clip 5: Demo: Inspect automation diffs in the Codex review pane (6 minutes)
•  Open an automation run that produced uncommitted changes and inspect the diff in the Codex review pane
•  Review changed files and hunks against the triage evidence that caused the automation to act
•  Use source control to stage valid hunks individually and revert an unrelated or incorrect hunk
•  Confirm only approved changes remain before the repository is committed
•  Learning Objectives: TO4, EO4a
Clip 6: Demo: Trace a failed Codex automation and recover safely (6 minutes)
•  Start from a failed automation result and trace the source evidence, generated change, and validation outcome
•  Use the review pane to isolate the incorrect hunk instead of discarding the entire run
•  Revert the bad change, preserve valid work, and rerun with corrected context
•  Verify the recovered run produces a clean reviewable diff before acceptance
•  Learning Objectives: TO4, EO4a
30 Mins
